meta.match_rule: Jev same_kind ≥ 2 (0-3 scale), as the push studies counted judge-passed replies; Part 1 only
notes: Olmo 3 only. Documents are gate-passed text (o3-weird-worlds docs.json, from gate-passed pulls; the rb1 pull of push-found writers' top documents); nothing held or quarantined; no ids, rows, URLs.
Highlights are [start, end, term] in Python code-point offsets, end exclusive (text with characters outside the BMP, e.g. emoji, needs code-point-aware slicing in JS: Array.from(text)).

Terms: words (>= 4 letters, no stop words) and capitalised word pairs in >= 2 of the neuron's documents and >= 1 of its replies, >= 10x more common in its documents than in the background (Part 1: all other weird-world and control documents; Part 2: all other rb1 documents); max 30.
Document text cut to 6000 characters (the neurons read the first 1,024 tokens).

Part 1 documents: the source's worlds2 set; half A ranked the neurons, half B (held out) measured zeroing. Replies: every push of the neuron at that pole across worlds1 and push2-9, every alpha; verdict = Jev same_kind score (0-3) per reply; the card's verdict is the blind consensus.

Part 2: the 224 writers (200 sampled + 24 known) of the rb1 read-back, whose top 20 documents per ranking went through the gate (1,542 of 34,684 rb1 documents were held and are missing). Replies: the writer screen's replies (ws1, ws2, cw1) and, for 8 writers, first-turn leading-question replies (ask2). The other ~1,180 screened writers have no pulled documents and are not included.

Card verdict: every Part 1 neuron is a blind-consensus writer (Claude Opus and Sonnet readers); Part 2 neurons passed the writer screen. Per-reply verdicts: Part 1 = Jev same_kind score and match (score >= match_threshold); Part 2 = null: the screen's judge saved only counts per neuron and strength (hits of 12 vs decoy hits), not which replies it picked.
Stage on a card: true / false / null (unchecked), from the o3-weird-worlds stage checks (as the sources chart); Part 2 top documents are stage-1 pretraining, mid/post presence unchecked (null).
Docs carry an extra `flags` list (content labels such as violence or hateful; not filtered out).
Controls: one unpushed reply per question (Part 1: from the push runs; Part 2: the screen's unpushed replies; cw1 questions have none).
